query: How can clinics improve triage and scheduling?

per_column.name: clinical_urgency_signal
per_column.rationale: Directly central to triage; a refined urgency axis beyond the coarse original 'urgency' column. Samples map soundly (preventive exam->preventive_wellness, MI follow-up->routine). Acne as 'semi_urgent' is a bit generous but defensible.

per_column.name: chief_complaint_category
per_column.rationale: Clinically meaningful grouping axis to analyze triage/scheduling patterns by complaint type. Categorizations are well-grounded in the reason_for_visit text across all samples.

per_column.name: presentation_acuity_type
per_column.rationale: New vs chronic vs preventive acuity is a strong axis for scheduling logic and distinct from urgency. Samples correctly derived (MI follow-up->chronic_stable_followup, cough->new_acute).

per_column.name: diagnostic_workup_required
per_column.rationale: Workup drives visit length and resource scheduling. Values well-grounded (labs->lab_ordered, MRI->imaging_ordered, viral URI->no_workup).

per_column.name: referral_or_consult_required
per_column.rationale: Referrals affect downstream scheduling/routing. Mostly grounded; the knee-MRI row labeled 'specialist_referral' is a mild inference since the text mentions imaging not an explicit referral, but reasonable.

per_column.name: in_visit_procedure_performed
per_column.rationale: Procedures affect slot duration and staffing—useful for scheduling. Samples correctly show no_procedure where text describes none; well-grounded.

per_column.name: follow_up_interval_signal
per_column.rationale: Follow-up cadence is directly actionable for scheduling. Mostly grounded; the annual-physical row labeled 'within_1_3_months' is slightly loose (labs ordered but no explicit interval), a minor stretch.

per_column.name: patient_population_context
per_column.rationale: Provides a demographic segmentation axis, but partially redundant with the existing age_group column, limiting new leverage. Inferred from age_group/department reasonably; acne->adult_reproductive_age is a plausible but somewhat speculative inference.

per_column.name: comorbidity_complexity_flag
per_column.rationale: Complexity is a useful predictor of visit length/scheduling needs. Grounding is weaker: the annual-physical row (mild fatigue, one abnormal BMI) labeled 'moderate_comorbidity' and MI follow-up as 'high_comorbidity' are inferential given only one documented condition each.

judge.rationale: The added columns collectively provide multiple genuine, non-redundant axes (refined urgency, complaint type, acuity, workup, referrals, procedures, follow-up cadence, complexity) that are directly relevant to improving triage and scheduling. Most values are soundly extracted or categorized from the reason_for_visit text. Groundedness is strong overall, with minor over-confident inferences in comorbidity_complexity_flag and a couple of follow-up/referral labels. patient_population_context is the weakest for usefulness due to overlap with the existing age_group column. No clear hallucinations observed.
